met-when.says: The original Code source receiver consumes NPM-registry-conformant archives and independently received Git source snapshots as explicitly distinguished source carriers through the same native product boundary. It preserves exact source bytes, executable intent, SRI and applicable provenance without requiring a Git repository for valid registry content. MetroPlat consumes these codecs through their original shared owners rather than adding a private archive, identity or publication implementation.

Original source acquisition and native product construction reuse held exact source objects, selected material and qualified dependency contexts by content identity. Unchanged source or a new task, retry or release identifier creates no second clone, dependency installation or provider payload copy. Current, rollback and necessary offline inputs remain usable.

The original Deployment Engine receives the original Code product and its actual programme command through a general engine with source, entry, unit, profile, data owner, providers and policies supplied as checked parameters. A replaced incumbent command is received separately from the incoming command; strings and opaque Guix inputs are compared only through their owning typed boundary. No publisher-specific substitute constructor, missing supplier module or metadata-only product claim grants activation.

Every selected generator, declaration reader, materializer and public entrance exists in the exact published supplier selected by its consumer before that consumer is qualified. Requirements generate specification, architecture, high-level design, low-level design and normative source through the original house generation chain, including the actual source language. Existing handwritten candidates are retained as unqualified inputs rather than relabeled as generated source.

Source, product and necessary evidence use the original content-address and custody owners. Observations use the shared SEAVT logger and original ledgers; they reference original source and product identities instead of recursively embedding repository trees, installations or repeated full provider graphs. Each producer retains its meaningful unpublished source and unresolved effects and owns terminal disposition after success, failure, cancellation and interruption.

The normal published source and installation paths on Bare Cedar Fog, its Windows and WSL consumers, Cold Red Gate and cloud consumers receive unchanged repetition, a one-input change, failed acquisition or installation, interruption and same-operation resumption, and rollback. Required capabilities remain available without reinstalling at service start. A merged change, source test, generated document, blanket hold, guest capacity check or new recovery route does not satisfy this operating condition.
